origin: Post-hoc hypotheses generated from the already-open EOG Azores endpoint; same-data tests are exploratory.
primary_question: In a strongly resident yellow-eel population, is temporal predictability generated primarily by persistent local residence, time-varying detectability/activity, or hydrologically synchronized pool dynamics?

hypotheses.name: persistent_local_state_memory
hypotheses.prediction: same-tag/same-pool previous state explains future detection; neighbour state adds little after local memory

hypotheses.name: activity_detection_memory
hypotheses.prediction: latent residence with time-varying detection explains detection gaps/reappearances better than observed-state switching

hypotheses.name: hydrological_reset
hypotheses.prediction: local-memory effect weakens during hydrological disturbance; memory-by-hydrology interaction is nonzero

hypotheses.name: shared_hydrological_synchrony
hypotheses.prediction: neighbour covariance attenuates after hydrological covariates
